x: The 880yds, probably the finest race of the Championships, seemed to be a struggle between Arthur Wint and the visiting New Zealand Champion Doug Harris until a few yards from the tape when both were overwhelmed by John Parlett's late surge.

Despite competing out of season against the in season Australian and New Zealand performers the Home Countries did well with fines wins by John Parlett in the 880 yds, Len Eyre in the 3 miles, Dorothy Tyler in the high jump, Tim Anderson in the pole vault and Jack Holden in the marathon.

The Great British middle distance event was of course dominated by Roger Bannister with new British mile and 1500 metre Records but perhaps a little disappointing in the Olympic Games. He was ably backed up by Bill Nankeville, four times British Champion, Len Eyre, John Parlett and Doug.
John Parlett was my schoolboy hero as we were from the same school and then of course there was Harry Churcher - one of the very best walkers I have known.
Gordon Pirie, Frank Sando, Alec Olney, John Parlett, Chris Chataway … these are just some of the stars of the ’50s & ’60s with whom Charlie tangled with over track, road and cross country.
